questions.q: In the scenario, why is x_abc_order_mgmt identified as the organization's highest-risk customization heading into the upgrade?
options: It combines high usage volume, a deprecated-API dependency flagged for removal, and a high blast radius if it breaks
It is the newest scoped application on the instance
It is owned by the team with the smallest headcount
It ships more frequently than the other two teams' applications
questions.explain: The lesson applies usage volume, deprecated-dependency risk, and blast radius together — all three point to this application as the top priority.

questions.q: Why does x_abc_order_mgmt get tested first in the pre-upgrade sandbox, rather than last?
options: Testing it first leaves maximum runway to fix any real blocker it reveals before the upgrade date
Testing order has no effect on how much time is available to fix issues
It must be tested first because it is alphabetically first among the three applications
Later testing is always preferred regardless of risk level
questions.explain: Finding a blocker in week one leaves months to fix it; finding the same blocker in the final week leaves no time to respond.

questions.q: Why is Team Fulfillment's quarterly release scheduled to land before the freeze window, rather than simply paused during it?
options: So their large batch of changes doesn't compete with upgrade validation for the same limited testing bandwidth during the freeze
Because quarterly releases are not allowed to be paused under any circumstances
Because Team Fulfillment's release has no connection to the upgrade testing process
Because the freeze window only applies to weekly-cadence teams
questions.explain: A release landing before the freeze means its changes get validated before the high-stakes upgrade testing period, rather than competing with it for the same bandwidth.

questions.q: How does the architect in this scenario decide the release freeze window, per the lesson's approach?
options: By proposing it early, publishing it on a shared calendar, and meeting individually with each team about what it costs them
By unilaterally mandating the freeze with no discussion with any team
By letting each team set its own separate freeze window independently
By canceling all three teams' releases for the entire four-month period
questions.explain: This follows Lesson 22's negotiated-governance approach rather than imposing one team's convenience on everyone else.

questions.q: What happens to Team Partner Integrations' unpredictable, partner-driven release cadence during the freeze window?
options: Emergency partner-driven changes go through an expedited, documented critical-fix path instead of a full release
All partner integration work is permanently canceled
The partner's API changes are simply ignored until after the upgrade
Team Partner Integrations is exempted from the freeze entirely with no process at all
questions.explain: Because the organization doesn't control the timing of the partner's API changes, the agreement provides a defined expedited path rather than ignoring the risk or granting an unstructured exemption.
